messages:
sophia: quick snapshot from this morning's bring-up sweep — ran 7b-newmodel (baseline: 13b-ref) across int8 / int4 quant configs. posting short econ + quality notes, need product/GTN recs on default & fallback.

sophia: tl;dr: int8 hits near-par quality with ~40% lower unit cost; int4 cuts cost ~65% but shows narrow regressions on long-form coherence and instruction-following. numbers below.

jordan: can you paste the eval command and dataset? want to reproduce.

sophia: sure — reproduce with:
```
python eval.py --model checkpoints/7b-newmodel --quant int8 --dataset eval/llama-like-instr-v2.jsonl --max_tokens 512 --seed 42 --out results/int8.jsonl
python eval.py --quant int4 --out results/int4.jsonl
```
we used 5k prompts (mix of instr+longform+code), holdout from prod promptset (w/ product edge cases). eval-bot: checksum 6a9f... attached.

lee: raw numbers? small table pls.

sophia: pasted summary (rounded):
- Quality (win-rate vs 13b-ref): int8 = 94%, int4 = 86%
- Avg Rouge-L / normalized: int8 = 0.88, int4 = 0.81, 13b-ref = 0.90
- Human eval: int8 passes 9/10 buckets (small delta), int4 fails 3 buckets (long coherence, step-by-step math, rare tokens)
- Latency (p50 / p95 token gen) on g5-16: int8 = 24ms / 78ms, int4 = 18ms / 64ms, 13b-ref = 38ms / 110ms
- Throughput (tokens/s per GPU): int8 1200, int4 1600, 13b-ref 650
- Unit cost (hosted token econ estimate): cost/token relative: 13b-ref=1.00, int8=0.60, int4=0.35

maria: those are promising. what's the distribution of prompt lengths? regression concentrated on >400 token outputs?

sophia: yes, regressions cluster when expected gen >350 tokens or tasks requiring sustained world-state (multi-step reasoning). short Q/A and code completion are fine for int4.

jordan: any calibration (e.g., temp, sampling) differences? int4 tuned with same decode params?

sophia: same decode params for parity. we also tried temp 0.2/0.7; quality gap persists for int4 at low temp in long-form cases.

lee: risk matrix for product/GTN:
- Interactive chat (SLAs <200ms p50): prefer int8 or 13b-ref for safety; int8 seems sweet spot given cost/latency tradeoff.
- Background summarization / embeddings prep: int4 is attractive.
- Billing-sensitive LTV flows: consider int4 with post-filtering & rerank by 13b-ref for flagged cases.

maria: routing idea: default route to int8 for "chat_low_latency" tier, fallback to 13b-ref when quality score < threshold or rare token triggers. For batch/async tasks, default int4 and sample 5% to int8 for QA.

sophia: suggested thresholds we tested: automatic rollback if eval win-rate drops >6% over baseline on canary; degrade-to-13b if human-fail-rate > 7% on production sample. Also: monitor top-k token entropy spikes as a cheap signal for hallucination.

jordan: what about unit econ impact for GTN pricing? any projection?

sophia: quick calc (hosted pricing model assumptions):
- baseline per-M token cost (13b-ref): $0.12
- int8 estimate: $0.072 (40% savings)
- int4 estimate: $0.042 (65% savings)
Example: product chat with avg 800 tokens/session -> cost/session: 13b=$0.096, int8=$0.0576, int4=$0.0336. At 100k sessions/mo, monthly delta = ~$2.4k (int8 vs 13b) and ~$6.24k (int4 vs 13b).

lee: nice. those are material for GTN comms. but beware quality churn causing retention issues — include holdback experiments.

maria: rollout plan proposal:
1) Canary 5% traffic -> int8 for chat_low_latency, monitor eval-bot metrics + human spot-checks for 48h.
2) If stable, ramp to 30% over a week; enable auto-fallback to 13b-ref on quality-signal.
3) For cost-focused routes (batch, background), enable int4 with conservative sampling (5-10%) to detect regressions.
4) Add a short eval suite in console (prod-alike prompts) with pass/fail gating before full rollout.

jordan: ops questions: memory & GPU packing differences for int4? can we 2x pack to save infra?

sophia: int4 allows denser packing — we tested 2x per-GPU on dedicated pools with minimal perf loss. need to validate on peak traffic.

eval-bot: automated note: canary test recipe saved at /evals/canary/7b-newmodel-int8.json. baseline artifact id: art-2026-03-10-7bref.

maria: final rec (for product ask): default to int8 on hosted & dedicated for interactive; enable int4 for background/low-priority tasks with sampling and rerank pipeline for critical outputs. include explicit fallback to 13b-ref when eval-gate fails. prepare one-pager for GTN with the cost examples above.

sophia: agreed. i'll draft the GTN one-pager and a minimal console eval set. tagging @jordan @lee for review before I send to product. :thumbsup:

jordan: will review. thanks for the concise numbers — super helpful.

lee: added a few notes in the canary recipe PR.

sophia: thanks all — closing thread after PR merges. :white_check_mark:
